records.name: Philcon
records.summary: A science fiction, fantasy and horror convention run by the Philadelphia Science Fiction Society, a nonprofit. It turns 90 in 2026 and depends on volunteers to staff its art show, stage tech, registration, gaming room and con suite.
records.what_you_do: Before the convention, volunteers help with publicity, social media, program planning or proofreading. During the convention, volunteers staff registration, run stage tech, load equipment in and out, and help with the art show, masquerade, green room, con suite and gaming room.

schedule.text: Annual convention on a Friday to Sunday weekend in the fall, at the DoubleTree by Hilton in Cherry Hill, New Jersey. Volunteer load-in starts the Thursday before.

locations.label: DoubleTree by Hilton, Cherry Hill, NJ
locations.address: 2349 Marlton Pike West, Cherry Hill, NJ

cost.text: Membership prices were not checked. Twelve volunteer hours earn a non-transferable rollover membership for next year, if you had a membership or volunteer rollover this year. Hours worked on the Thursday or Friday before 3 pm, or on Sunday from 4 pm on, count double.

access.notes: The convention FAQ says the hotel's sleeping rooms, restrooms and event rooms are wheelchair accessible, with one exception it does not name. Elevators serve every event floor except the first. Only service animals are allowed; pets are not.

first_step.how: Email volunteers@philcon.org before the convention with what you would like to help with, or go to the Crystal 1 office during the event and tell the first desk you want to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says most roles need no experience and that the convention trains volunteers, and it gives two clear ways to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: You can volunteer as much or as little as you like, and the volunteer page does not list shift lengths. Before the event you might help with publicity, proofreading or programming. During the event you could staff registration or the office, help with tech for the main stage, or work at the art show, gaming room or con suite. Each volunteer signs a liability release, and department heads sign off on an hours log.
first_visit_tips: Download the volunteer release form from the volunteering page. Minors need a parent or guardian to sign it.
Keep your hours log current, since department heads sign off on your hours.
Hotel parking is free and mostly covered, according to the FAQ.
If you are under 16, come with a parent or legal guardian, as the FAQ requires.

records.notes: Convention is in Cherry Hill, NJ, so in_city is false. The group is a Philadelphia science fiction society, so the orchestrator should decide whether it counts as serving Philadelphia; kept as publish. The volunteer page and FAQ do not cover background checks, shift lengths, or a minimum age for volunteers beyond the parent signature rule. Wheelchair is partial because the FAQ names one unspecified exception. Schedule text drops the 2026 dates, which belong in last_sign_of_life. Homepage facts were carried from tier 1 and not re-read this run.

records.name: Philly 2600
records.summary: A monthly public meetup for people interested in technology and computer security. Attendees can use a pseudonym, and bringing friends is welcome.
records.what_you_do: Come to the first Friday meeting in person to talk about technology and security with other attendees. Some people go on to a nearby bar or restaurant afterward.

schedule.text: First Friday of every month. People usually arrive around 6 pm and stay until about 8:30 pm.

cost.text: The site does not mention a cost.

first_step.how: Come to the first Friday meeting at Iffy Books, 404 S 20th St, around 6 pm. The site lists no sign-up step.
first_step.basis: The site says to come as you are, that you can join in or just listen, and that a pseudonym is fine. There is no sign-up step, but the page does not use the word beginner.
first_step.what_to_expect: Arrive any time around 6 pm and leave when you like. Talk breaks into several small groups at once, on topics such as hacking, sysadmin work and security, and you can join in or just listen. You do not need a topic or a real name, and guests are welcome. The after-meeting venue may be 21 and over, and under-21 attendees can ask the group to find a suitable place.
first_visit_tips: Check the group's Mastodon link for location changes before you go, since the site's blog shows no dated posts after 2016.
Use a nickname if you like, since the group does not ask for real names.
Under-21 attendees can tell the group ahead of time so it can find a suitable after-meeting place.
Guests are welcome, so you can bring a friend.

records.notes: Status set to unknown, not probably_active: the meeting page has no dates, the blog's newest dated post is from April 2016, and the Mastodon account showed no posts when read. Under the status rule this could be dormant, so the orchestrator may decide. The meeting page reads partly garbled and has no cost, accessibility or parking details. Iffy Books is a business venue, not a group, so it is not a lead. Crowd and kids_ok come from the site's line that the group is open to all ages.

records.name: Philly Bluegrass
records.summary: A Philadelphia area group for bluegrass and roots music players and fans, with shows and open jams. It runs a newsletter and sells merch, and its Center City jam welcomes beginners.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly Center City jam after an RSVP to play or listen, go to a show, or join the mailing list for news about jams and shows.

schedule.text: Center City jam on the second Thursday of each month, 7 to 9 pm. The location is sent after you RSVP. Other jams and shows in the region are listed on the calendar.

locations.label: Center City jam (location sent after RSVP)

cost.text: No admission fee is listed for the jam. The group takes optional donations, which are tax deductible.

first_step.how: Email the RSVP contact listed on the group's FAQ page to get the jam location, then go on the second Thursday to play or listen.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says beginners are welcome and encouraged at the Center City jam and gives a clear RSVP route. The venue is shared only after an RSVP, so you cannot just show up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The jam runs two hours, 7 to 9 pm, on the second Thursday of the month. You get the venue only after you RSVP. The group welcomes beginners, but the pages do not say whether you need your own instrument or whether there is any charge.
first_visit_tips: RSVP ahead of time, since the venue is shared only after you reply.
Ask when you RSVP whether to bring an instrument, because the pages do not say.
If the Center City date does not suit you, the calendar lists other jams and shows across the region.

records.notes: The homepage capture did not show the Center City jam, but the Get Involved page and the FAQ both name it, so the tier 1 detail is kept. The RSVP address on those pages looks like a personal email account, so it is not recorded; the orchestrator may decide whether to publish it. The homepage's other October 2026 events are jams in Highland Park NJ, Perkasie and Doylestown (outside Philadelphia) and shows, and were not recorded. The calendar page's event listings did not load, so its events are unchecked.

records.name: Philly Game Mechanics
records.summary: An indie game making group in Philadelphia that welcomes hobbyists, students and pros. It runs playtest nights, game jams and workshops, announced through its newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Join the Discord chat, show a game at a playtest night, take part in a game jam or workshop when one is announced, or sign up for the newsletter.

schedule.text: A monthly Playtest Night is the group's regular event. Game jams, workshops, coffee meetups, hikes and happy hours come up through the year and are announced in its news posts. The events page currently lists no dated events.

cost.text: The site does not state event costs.

first_step.how: Join the Discord chat, or sign up for the newsletter, to hear about the next monthly Playtest Night or game jam.
first_step.basis: The home page says the group supports developers at every level and names a Discord chat and a newsletter as ways in, but it does not say whether events are open to the public.
first_step.what_to_expect: Playtest Nights are where creators show a game in progress and get feedback from other developers. Game jams are short builds that run from a few days to a few weeks. The site does not say whether events are open to the public, what they cost, or where they meet, so check the Discord or newsletter for details before you go.
first_visit_tips: Say hello in the Discord first, since it is the group's main way to connect with members.
Ask in the Discord whether a playtest night is open to newcomers before you go.
If you have a game to test, bring it to a playtest night, where creators show their games and get feedback.
The group also posts on Meetup, which may list dates that the website does not.

records.notes: Status is active from the news page, whose latest item is dated November 16, 2025. The events page lists no dated events, and the home page's only dated item is a game release, not a group event. A May fundraiser with a 2026 goal is not counted as activity. Playtest Night venues are announced per event. Meetup was not read (lead source only). IGDA is named as a 2025 partner with no URL, so it is not a lead.

records.name: Philly HEALs Grief Support Groups
records.summary: The City of Philadelphia's bereavement program for people grieving a loss linked to substance use. It runs free online peer groups.
records.what_you_do: Pick the peer group that fits your loss from the city's list: a drop-in group, a parents group, Hot Widows' Club, GRANDS, Hay Otros en Duelo (a group with a Spanish name), and Writing Grief, a time-limited group that uses creative writing. The program also offers grief counseling for adults and youth, and workshops.

schedule.text: Peer groups are held online, mostly by phone or video call, with some in-person events now and then. The city page does not list meeting days or times for each group, so ask through the sign-up survey which group fits and when it meets.

cost.text: Free, with no insurance needed, according to the program page.

first_step.how: Use the sign-up survey linked from the city's grief support page to ask which peer group fits your loss, or call the program line at 215-516-9429.
first_step.basis: Open to people grieving a Philadelphia resident's substance-related death, with a clear first step (a sign-up survey or a phone call), though the pages do not say what happens after the survey.
first_step.what_to_expect: The city page does not give meeting times for each group or describe a typical session, so ask the program what the first meetings look like. Peer groups meet online, usually by video or phone. The program is free and needs no insurance.
first_visit_tips: Ask the program which group fits your loss, since the pages do not explain how the groups differ.
Find a quiet, private spot with a reliable connection for an online group.
The city page lists 988 (24 hours) for crisis help, and the NAMI Philadelphia Warmline at (844) 745-4673, weekdays 9 am to 5 pm, for support between groups.

records.notes: Correction to tier 1: neither page says Hay Otros en Duelo is a Spanish-language group, so the record notes only the Spanish name. The city page lists no meeting times per group. The Healthy Minds Philly November 2026 calendar lists one Philly HEALs group (a virtual group called All Arms Locked, on three November dates); other November support listings come from other organizations and are not recorded. The program manager's named contact and direct email are left out; the program phone line is used. The Substance Use Philly page names other grief groups, listed in leads_only.

records.name: Philly JS Club
records.summary: Philadelphia developers who work with JavaScript and the web. Most months they meet at Indy Hall for short talks, hack nights, and project showcases.
records.what_you_do: Listen to talks on web tools and frameworks, bring a project to a hack night, show what you built, and meet other developers.

schedule.text: Usually once a month, most often on the second Thursday, at Indy Hall for a talk, hack night or showcase. The events page lists the dates.

cost.text: The events page does not list a cost, and the About page does not mention fees.

first_step.how: Pick the next talk or hack night on the events page and go; if its listing has an RSVP link, use it first. You can also fill in the sign-up form linked from the Join Us page.
first_step.basis: The About page says the club is for developers of all skill and experience levels, and the Join Us page links a sign-up form. Some listings link to RSVP pages.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings are usually once a month, most often on a Thursday, at Indy Hall. Expect a short talk on a web tool or framework, time to meet other developers, and, at some meetings, a hack night or a showcase of what members built. The events page does not give start times, and some listings use RSVP pages.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the date, and whether the listing asks you to RSVP.
If you go to a hack night, bring a project or idea you want to work on.
The events page does not give street addresses or start times, so email organizers@phillyjs.com before you go if you need them.

records.notes: The events page lists talks, hack nights and showcases every month from January 2025 through September 2026, almost always on the second Thursday, which is the pattern the schedule text names. Age rules, the code of conduct text, and a street address for Indy Hall were not on the pages read. DataPhilly, PhillyCHI and Technical.ly appear on the events page as co-hosts or past hosts, with no URLs, so they are not leads.

records.name: Philly Mah-Jawn Mahjong Club
records.summary: A Philadelphia mahjong club that meets every week for players of all levels. It has a clubhouse in Old City, teaches newcomers, and its president said in August 2026 that weekly crowds had grown to about 50 people.
records.what_you_do: Learn to play mahjong, including the Japanese riichi style, join the weekly play, and take part in club tournaments.

schedule.text: Weekly play. A July 2025 news report listed clubhouse sessions on Friday evenings (7 to 11 pm), Saturdays (noon to 8 pm) and Sundays (2 to 8 pm), plus Wednesday evenings (6:30 to 10 pm) at the King of Prussia Bridge Club. Times may have changed, and 2026 reports say weekly meetups also happen at board game cafes.

locations.label: Clubhouse, second floor of the Corn Exchange Building, Old City
Board game cafes (weekly meetups, per August 2026 report)
King of Prussia Bridge Club (Wednesday sessions)

cost.text: An introductory membership is $20 for the year. Members then pay $10 for each day they play, and non-members pay the $10 day fee at the Saturday teaching block. A $60 yearly membership adds a stamp card that makes the 10th visit free and access to members-only tournaments. Figures are from a July 2025 news report.

first_step.how: Go to a session and ask for a lesson. A 2025 news report named a walk-in teaching block on Saturdays from noon to 2 pm, so check the club's website for current times first.
first_step.basis: Recent news says volunteers teach brand-new visitors at meetups and the club holds lessons, and a 2025 news report describes a weekly Saturday walk-in teaching block for players of all levels. The article does not say whether you must reserve a spot.
first_step.what_to_expect: Newcomers can take part with volunteers or officers teaching the game to walk-in visitors. The club holds lessons, and some members enter club tournaments. Non-members pay a $10 day fee at the Saturday teaching block, according to the 2025 report. The news reports do not say how long a visit lasts.
first_visit_tips: Ask for a lesson as soon as you arrive, since volunteers teach first-time visitors.
Expect a $10 day fee if you are not a member, according to the 2025 report.
The clubhouse is on the second floor, and the reports do not say whether there is an elevator, so ask before you go.
Check the club's website first, because the 2025 hours may have changed and 2026 reports name board game cafes as meetup places.

records.notes: Two 2026 news reports disagree on where weekly play happens and how big it is: May 2026 (about 15 to 20 members at the Old City clubhouse) and August 2026 (50 to 55 people at board game cafes). The clubhouse address also differs: 2nd and Chestnut Streets in TV coverage, 123 Chestnut Street, 19106 in a Philly Mag listing. Schedule and cost figures come from a July 2025 Billy Penn article and may be out of date. The club website returned only its title on two reads, so nothing from it is recorded beyond the URL. The Philly Mag listing and a search summary both mention a Saturday newcomer session and a Wednesday King of Prussia session, which matches the 2025 article.

notes: Seven batch groups, all kept as publish. Searches: 1 of 1 used (hard cap). Fetches: 23 of 60 used, never more than 6 on one group. No rate limiting or bot checks seen; the phillymahjong.com homepage and the Mastodon account (jawns.club/@philly2600) returned only a title or header, so nothing was taken from them. Status changes: philly-2600 moved from probably_active to unknown (its meeting page has no dates, its blog's newest dated post is April 2016, and its Mastodon feed showed no posts when read); philly-game-mechanics moved to active on its news page (latest item November 2025). Corrections: the city's Philly HEALs page does not say Hay Otros en Duelo is Spanish-language, so the record notes only the Spanish name. Philly Bluegrass: the RSVP address on its FAQ and Get Involved pages looks like a personal email account, so it is not recorded in contacts; the orchestrator may decide. Philly HEALs: the program manager's named contact and direct email were left out; the program phone line is used. Philcon's convention is in Cherry Hill, NJ, so the orchestrator should decide whether it fits the city scope; kept as publish. Leads: the Philly HEALs partner list names more grief groups with their own websites (see leads_only). They are not fetched in this run: this lane's brief sends partner names to leads_only for later tier 1 checks, and several are national or based outside Philadelphia. Nar-Anon Family Groups was named without a URL in the page summary, so it is not listed. Not leads: Iffy Books, Indy Hall and other venues (businesses, not groups); DataPhilly, PhillyCHI, Technical.ly and IGDA were named without URLs.
